_note: Audited JAMB Government starter bank. Every item comes from the 2020 paper; the key was checked by hand, wording was lightly cleaned, and each item has a topic tag and explanation. Items with wrong keys or defective options were rejected rather than guessed.
subject: government

questions.question: An example of a country with an unwritten constitution is ______.
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom has no single written constitutional document; its constitution is found in statutes, common law and conventions.

questions.question: The rule of law is only applicable in ______.

options.text: in states where laws are supreme

questions.explanation: The rule of law requires everyone, including the government, to be subject to the law. It operates where laws are supreme.

questions.question: The legislative arm of government is ______.
questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws; the executive implements them and the judiciary interprets them.

questions.question: The fundamental laws of a country are contained in its ______.
questions.explanation: A constitution contains the fundamental laws that establish and limit government.

questions.question: The Crown Colony of Lagos was created in ______.
questions.explanation: Lagos was annexed as a Crown Colony in 1861.

questions.question: All these are civil obligations of every Nigerian citizen except ______.

options.text: respect for the national anthem and flag

questions.explanation: Freedom of conscience is a civil liberty, not an obligation. Obedience to law, respect for national symbols and payment of tax are duties.

questions.question: The Lyttleton Constitution is important because it ______.

options.text: abolished the principle of indirect rule
confirmed Nigeria as a federal structure

questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 confirmed Nigeria as a federation with regional premiers and a division of powers.

questions.question: An important advantage of a public corporation is that it ______.

options.text: makes quick profit at the expense of the people
render crucial services to the people in areas which the civil service cannot effectively handle

questions.explanation: Public corporations deliver essential services in areas where the civil service or private firms cannot operate effectively.

questions.question: The British Government revoked the charter of the Royal Niger Company and took over the direct administration of Nigeria in ______.
questions.explanation: In 1900 Britain revoked the Royal Niger Company charter and took direct control of Nigeria.

questions.question: A bill becomes an Act of Parliament after it has been ______.

options.text: Signed by the head of state
processed through the committee of the house

questions.explanation: A bill becomes an Act after the head of state assents to it. Debate, committee work and passage are earlier stages.

questions.question: Which of these international organisations was the predecessor of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The League of Nations (1920–1946) was the predecessor of the United Nations.

questions.question: Nigeria's withdrawal from the Edinburgh Commonwealth Games in July 1986 was in protest against British ______.

options.text: support for UNITA rebels in Angola
failure to impose sanctions on South Africa's apartheid government

questions.explanation: Nigeria withdrew from the 1986 Edinburgh Commonwealth Games to protest Britain's failure to impose sanctions on apartheid South Africa.

questions.question: The major difference between the presidential and parliamentary systems is ______.
questions.explanation: The presidential system separates the executive from the legislature; the parliamentary system fuses them, and the executive depends on parliamentary confidence.

questions.question: The Nigerian who once served as President of the United Nations General Assembly was ______.
questions.explanation: Joseph Garba was President of the UN General Assembly in 1973–74.

questions.question: The 1976 local government reforms were a benefit to ______.
questions.explanation: The 1976 reforms gave local governments a uniform structure and direct federal funding, strengthening the third tier.

questions.question: The Galadima in the emirate system was ______.

options.text: Officer in charge of the army

questions.explanation: The Galadima administered the capital of an emirate under the Emir.

questions.question: A vote taken by the citizenry of a country on an important political issue is a ______.
questions.explanation: A referendum is a direct vote by the electorate on a specific political issue.

questions.question: A major feature of a confederal state is that ______.

options.text: there is supremacy of the constitution
The citizens often owe allegiance to the center

questions.explanation: Confederal states are often unstable because the centre depends on the goodwill of the constituent units.

questions.question: In the modern local government structure in Nigeria, traditional rulers play ______.
questions.explanation: Traditional rulers advise modern local governments; they do not legislate or execute.

questions.question: The Nigeria–Cameroon crisis over the Bakassi Peninsula was subject to the decision of ______.

options.text: decision of the International Court of Justice

questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice decided the Bakassi Peninsula dispute in favour of Cameroon in 2002.

questions.question: Under Nigeria's 1999 Constitution, the power to nominate members of the judiciary at the federal level is vested in the ______.
questions.explanation: The Federal Judicial Service Commission nominates federal judicial officers for appointment.

questions.question: The most senior member of the council of elders in the Igbo political system was the ______.
questions.explanation: The Okpara, the oldest man in the village, headed the Igbo council of elders.

questions.question: The country that withdrew her membership of ECOWAS is ______.
questions.explanation: Mauritania withdrew from ECOWAS in 2000.

questions.question: The traditional political system of the Yoruba kingdom was ______.
questions.explanation: Yoruba kingdoms were monarchical, with an Oba at the head of each kingdom.

questions.question: The nationalist movements in Nigeria and the Gold Coast (Ghana) ______.

options.text: produced the same result in both countries.

questions.explanation: Nationalist movements in Nigeria and the Gold Coast influenced each other significantly.

questions.question: The Ogboni cult in the pre-colonial Yoruba political system played the role of ______.
questions.explanation: The Ogboni cult performed judicial and religious functions in the pre-colonial Yoruba system.

questions.question: Military intervention in Nigeria was a result of ______.

options.text: perceived incapability of civilians to govern
the desire for a military government.

questions.explanation: Military coups were justified by the perceived inability of civilian governments to govern effectively.

questions.question: A system of government ruled by old people is known as ______.
questions.explanation: Gerontocracy is rule by the elderly.

questions.question: All the following ethnic groups in Northern Nigeria had their pre-colonial political structure influenced by Islamic culture except ______.
questions.explanation: The Tiv were not significantly influenced by Islamic culture, unlike the Kanuri, Fulani and Nupe.

questions.question: Nigeria is a member of the following international organisations except ______.
questions.explanation: Nigeria belongs to ECOWAS, the Commonwealth and OPEC, but not NATO.

questions.question: The motion for Nigeria's independence was moved by ______.
questions.explanation: Chief Anthony Enahoro moved the motion for independence in 1953.

questions.question: According to the 1979 Constitution, to be elected president one must have attained the age of ______.
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution set the minimum age for president at 35 years.

questions.question: The supremacy of the legislature exists in ______.
questions.explanation: In Britain Parliament is supreme: the legislature can make or unmake any law.

questions.question: The system of government where power derives from total control of the instruments of force is ______.
questions.explanation: Fascism relies on total control of the instruments of force and subordinates the individual to the state.

questions.question: Indirect rule in Nigeria encouraged ______.
questions.explanation: Indirect rule exposed Nigerians to colonial exploitation and helped spark the rise of nationalism.

questions.question: Nigeria's first executive president was ______.
questions.explanation: Shehu Shagari became Nigeria’s first executive president in 1979.

questions.question: The executive checks the excesses of the legislature through ______.
questions.explanation: The executive veto lets the president reject bills passed by the legislature.

questions.question: The development of a classless society is the goal of ______.
questions.explanation: Marxism aims at a classless, communist society.

questions.question: Which of the following states were created in 1996?
questions.explanation: Gombe and Ekiti were among the six states created in 1996.

questions.question: The review of Nigeria's foreign policy under the Murtala/Obasanjo regime was done by ______.
questions.explanation: The Adedeji Commission reviewed Nigeria’s foreign policy under the Murtala/Obasanjo regime.
